context.title: Storm and Shipwreck
context.summary: Paul sails for Rome under guard. Ignoring his warning, the crew leaves port late in the season and is caught in a violent storm. After two weeks adrift, all 276 aboard reach land safely when the ship breaks apart off Malta.
context.background: Sea travel became dangerous by mid-September and largely stopped for winter. 'The fast' (v. 9) is the Day of Atonement, in late September or October, so they were already in the risky season. Alexandrian grain ships like this one carried Egypt's wheat to Rome.

customs.note: Sailors passed ropes or cables around the hull to hold the timbers together in heavy seas.

watchFor: The vivid 'we' narration of a firsthand voyage.
Paul goes from prisoner to the one everyone listens to (vv. 21–26, 31–36).
Paul gives thanks and breaks bread before them all (v. 35).

people.name: Paul
people.summary: Saul was born about the same time as our Lord. His circumcision-name was Saul, and probably the name Paul was also given to him in infancy “for use in the Gentile world,” as “Saul” would be his Hebrew home-name.

people.name: Julius
people.summary: The centurion of the Augustan cohort, or the emperor’s body-guard, in whose charge Paul was sent prisoner to Rome (Acts 27:1, 3, 43).

people.name: Aristarchus
people.summary: Best ruler, native of Thessalonica (Acts 20:4), a companion of Paul (Acts 19:29; 27:2).

places.name: Italy
places.summary: Acts 18:2; 27:1, 6; Heb. 13:24), like most geographical names, was differently used at different periods of history. As the power of Rome advanced, nations were successively conquered and added to it till it came to designate the whole country to the south of the Alps.

places.name: Adramyttium
places.summary: A city of Asia Minor on the coast of Mysia, which in early times was called AEolis. The ship in which Paul embarked at Caesarea belonged to this city (Acts 27:2).

places.name: Asia
places.summary: Is used to denote Proconsular Asia, a Roman province which embraced the western parts of Asia Minor, and of which Ephesus was the capital, in Acts 2:9; 6:9; 16:6; 19:10, 22; 20:4, 16, 18, etc., and probably Asia Minor in Acts 19:26, 27; 21:27; 24:18; 27:2.

places.name: Thessalonica
places.summary: A large and populous city on the Thermaic bay. It was the capital of one of the four Roman districts of Macedonia, and was ruled by a praetor.

places.name: Sidon
places.summary: A fishery, a town on the Mediterranean coast, about 25 miles north of Tyre. It received its name from the “first-born” of Canaan, the grandson of Noah (Gen. 10:15, 19).

places.name: Cyprus
places.summary: One of the largest islands of the Mediterranean, about 148 miles long and 40 broad. It is distant about 60 miles from the Syrian coast. It was the “Chittim” of the Old Testament (Num. 24:24).

places.name: Cilicia
places.summary: A maritime province in the south-east of Asia Minor. Tarsus, the birth-place of Paul, was one of its chief towns, and the seat of a celebrated school of philosophy.

places.name: Lycia
places.summary: A wolf, a province in the south-west of Asia Minor, opposite the island of Rhodes. It forms part of the region now called Tekeh. It was a province of the Roman empire when visited by Paul (Acts 21:1; 27:5).

places.name: Myra
places.summary: One of the chief towns of Lycia, in Asia Minor, about 2 1/2 miles from the coast (Acts 27:5).

places.name: Pamphylia
places.summary: Paul and his company, loosing from Paphos, sailed north-west and came to Perga, the capital of Pamphylia (Acts 13:13, 14), a province about the middle of the southern sea-board of Asia Minor.

places.name: Alexandria
places.summary: The ancient metropolis of Lower Egypt, so called from its founder, Alexander the Great (about B.C. 333). It was for a long period the greatest of existing cities, for both Nineveh and Babylon had been destroyed, and Rome had not yet risen to greatness.

places.name: Cnidus
places.summary: A town and harbour on the extreme south-west of the peninsula of Doris in Asia Minor.

places.name: Crete
places.summary: Now called Candia, one of the largest islands in the Meditterranean, about 140 miles long and 35 broad. It was at one time a very prosperous and populous island, having a “hundred cities.”

places.name: Salmone
places.summary: A promontory on the east of Crete, under which Paul sailed on his voyage to Rome (Acts 27:7); the modern Cape Sidero.

places.name: Fair Havens
places.summary: A harbour in the south of Crete, some 5 miles to the east of which was the town of Lasea (Acts 27:8). Here the ship of Alexandria in which Paul and his companions sailed was detained a considerable time waiting for a favourable wind.

places.name: Lasea
places.summary: A city in the island of Crete (Acts 27:8).

places.name: Phenice
places.summary: Properly Phoenix a palm-tree (as in the R.V.), a town with a harbour on the southern side of Crete (Acts 27:12), west of the Fair Havens.

places.name: Clauda
places.summary: A small island off the southwest coast of Crete, passed by Paul on his voyage to Rome (Acts 27:16). It is about 7 miles long and 3 broad.

places.name: Syrtis
places.summary: Found only in Acts 27:17, the rendering of the Greek Syrtis. On the north coast of Africa were two localities dangerous to sailors, called the Greater and Lesser Syrtis.

places.name: Adria
places.summary: (Acts 27:27; R.V., “the sea of Adria”), the Adriatic Sea, including in Paul’s time the whole of the Mediterranean lying between Crete and Sicily.

events.title: Journey to Rome begins
events.summary: Passage: Acts 27:1–12. People: Aristarchus, Julius, Paul, Luke. Place: Phenice, Lasea, Fair Havens, Crete.

events.title: Paul's Journey to Rome
events.summary: Passage: Acts 27:1–28:31. People: Paul, Luke, Aristarchus, Julius. Place: Phenice, Lasea, Fair Havens, Crete. Lasted about 4 years.

events.title: Paul is shipwrecked by a storm
events.summary: Passage: Acts 27:13–44. People: Paul, Julius, Aristarchus, Luke. Place: Adria, Syrtis, Clauda, Crete.
